violations_found.violations:
- Organizational Constraint violated: The narrative states the EU pushes forward "five measures", but Constitutional Constraint 5 limits the EU to at most one new measure per turn. The notepad lists three ongoing measures (InvestAI Gigafactories, Resilience Acceleration Programme, Joint Access Framework Implementation) and a priority charge, but introducing more than one new measure in a single turn—especially one large category 6 initiative among others—exceeds the limit. The proposal bonus section implies multiple new measures are being introduced ("pushes forward five measures, including the new large category 6 initiative"), which violates the "at most one new measure per turn" rule.
- Economic Constraint violated: The Resilience Acceleration Programme is described as a large category 6 initiative with €12bn in funding, but no identified source of financing is provided. Large-cost measures require a minimum of two full turns for implementation (Constitutional Constraint 6), and such a significant expenditure must be justified by revenue, reallocation, or borrowing. The update assumes immediate allocation without demonstrating budgetary feasibility or phasing.
- Regulatory Constraint violated: The Resilience Acceleration Programme is announced and already contributing +3 to resilience in the same turn it is launched. However, Constitutional Constraint 6 ("No measure is implemented instantly") requires a minimum of one full turn for low-cost measures and two for high-cost ones. A category 6 (large) measure cannot have any effect this quickly; even partial effects are inconsistent with the minimum lead time.
